# Lab 26.7: Respond to a Compromised Service Account

## What We Are Going to Do
Walk through a leaked service account key: contain it, find what it did, remove persistence and prevent it from happening again.

## Steps

1. **Set the scene.** Create a service account and key to act as the "leaked" one.


<div style="margin:18px 0;border:1px solid #334155;border-radius:8px;overflow:hidden;">
<div style="background:#243244;color:#DBEAFE;padding:7px 12px;font-family:Segoe UI,Arial,sans-serif;font-size:12px;font-weight:700;">
CODE • BASH
</div>
<pre style="margin:0;background:#111827;color:#F3F4F6;padding:16px;overflow-x:auto;white-space:pre;font-family:Consolas,'Cascadia Code',monospace;font-size:14px;line-height:1.55;"><code><span style="color:#F3F4F6;">gcloud iam service-accounts create leaked-sa
gcloud projects add-iam-policy-binding $PROJECT_ID \
  --member=serviceAccount:leaked-sa@$PROJECT_ID.iam.gserviceaccount.com --role=roles/storage.admin
gcloud iam service-accounts keys create leaked.json \
  --iam-account=leaked-sa@$PROJECT_ID.iam.gserviceaccount.com
gcloud auth activate-service-account --key-file=leaked.json
gcloud storage buckets create gs://$PROJECT_ID-attacker-test --location=us-central1
gcloud config set account YOUR_EMAIL</span>
</code></pre>
</div>


2. **Contain: disable the key and the account.**


<div style="margin:18px 0;border:1px solid #334155;border-radius:8px;overflow:hidden;">
<div style="background:#243244;color:#DBEAFE;padding:7px 12px;font-family:Segoe UI,Arial,sans-serif;font-size:12px;font-weight:700;">
CODE • BASH
</div>
<pre style="margin:0;background:#111827;color:#F3F4F6;padding:16px;overflow-x:auto;white-space:pre;font-family:Consolas,'Cascadia Code',monospace;font-size:14px;line-height:1.55;"><code><span style="color:#F3F4F6;">gcloud iam service-accounts keys list --iam-account=leaked-sa@$PROJECT_ID.iam.gserviceaccount.com --managed-by=user
gcloud iam service-accounts keys disable KEY_ID --iam-account=leaked-sa@$PROJECT_ID.iam.gserviceaccount.com
gcloud iam service-accounts disable leaked-sa@$PROJECT_ID.iam.gserviceaccount.com</span>
</code></pre>
</div>


   Disabling is fast and reversible. If the account is needed by production, use a deny policy on risky permissions instead.

3. **Investigate: what did it do?**


<div style="margin:18px 0;border:1px solid #334155;border-radius:8px;overflow:hidden;">
<div style="background:#243244;color:#DBEAFE;padding:7px 12px;font-family:Segoe UI,Arial,sans-serif;font-size:12px;font-weight:700;">
CODE • BASH
</div>
<pre style="margin:0;background:#111827;color:#F3F4F6;padding:16px;overflow-x:auto;white-space:pre;font-family:Consolas,'Cascadia Code',monospace;font-size:14px;line-height:1.55;"><code><span style="color:#F3F4F6;">gcloud logging read \
  'protoPayload.authenticationInfo.principalEmail="leaked-sa@'$PROJECT_ID'.iam.gserviceaccount.com"' \
  --freshness=7d \
  --format="table(timestamp,protoPayload.methodName,protoPayload.resourceName,protoPayload.requestMetadata.callerIp)"</span>
</code></pre>
</div>


   Note the caller IPs and every resource it created or changed.

4. **Look for persistence.** Attackers often create new keys, new service accounts or new IAM grants.


<div style="margin:18px 0;border:1px solid #334155;border-radius:8px;overflow:hidden;">
<div style="background:#243244;color:#DBEAFE;padding:7px 12px;font-family:Segoe UI,Arial,sans-serif;font-size:12px;font-weight:700;">
CODE • TEXT
</div>
<pre style="margin:0;background:#111827;color:#F3F4F6;padding:16px;overflow-x:auto;white-space:pre;font-family:Consolas,'Cascadia Code',monospace;font-size:14px;line-height:1.55;"><code><span style="color:#F3F4F6;">protoPayload.methodName=("google.iam.admin.v1.CreateServiceAccountKey" OR "google.iam.admin.v1.CreateServiceAccount" OR "SetIamPolicy")</span>
</code></pre>
</div>


5. **Eradicate.** Delete what the attacker created, delete the key, and remove broad roles.


<div style="margin:18px 0;border:1px solid #334155;border-radius:8px;overflow:hidden;">
<div style="background:#243244;color:#DBEAFE;padding:7px 12px;font-family:Segoe UI,Arial,sans-serif;font-size:12px;font-weight:700;">
CODE • BASH
</div>
<pre style="margin:0;background:#111827;color:#F3F4F6;padding:16px;overflow-x:auto;white-space:pre;font-family:Consolas,'Cascadia Code',monospace;font-size:14px;line-height:1.55;"><code><span style="color:#F3F4F6;">gcloud storage rm --recursive gs://$PROJECT_ID-attacker-test
gcloud iam service-accounts keys delete KEY_ID --iam-account=leaked-sa@$PROJECT_ID.iam.gserviceaccount.com --quiet
gcloud projects remove-iam-policy-binding $PROJECT_ID \
  --member=serviceAccount:leaked-sa@$PROJECT_ID.iam.gserviceaccount.com --role=roles/storage.admin
rm leaked.json</span>
</code></pre>
</div>


6. **Prevent it.** Enforce `iam.disableServiceAccountKeyCreation`, move workloads to Workload Identity Federation or attached service accounts, and turn on SCC notifications for key-related findings.

7. **Clean up.**


<div style="margin:18px 0;border:1px solid #334155;border-radius:8px;overflow:hidden;">
<div style="background:#243244;color:#DBEAFE;padding:7px 12px;font-family:Segoe UI,Arial,sans-serif;font-size:12px;font-weight:700;">
CODE • BASH
</div>
<pre style="margin:0;background:#111827;color:#F3F4F6;padding:16px;overflow-x:auto;white-space:pre;font-family:Consolas,'Cascadia Code',monospace;font-size:14px;line-height:1.55;"><code><span style="color:#F3F4F6;">gcloud iam service-accounts delete leaked-sa@$PROJECT_ID.iam.gserviceaccount.com --quiet</span>
</code></pre>
</div>


## Expected Result

| Thing | Reality |
|---|---|
| Containment | Key and account disabled in minutes |
| Investigation | Audit logs filtered by the account |
| Persistence | New keys, accounts and grants checked |
| Prevention | No keys, WIF instead |
